title: The 10 Best Laser Levels
subtitle: Self-leveling cross-line and 360-degree laser levels for hanging pictures, cabinets, tile and ceilings, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A self-leveling laser projects a level (and plumb) line across a wall or a whole room, so you can hang a row of cabinets or tile a backsplash without a 4-foot level and a pencil. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a green beam, full 360-degree lines, a rechargeable battery, a pulse mode for outdoor detectors and a tripod in the box). Cross-line lasers cover one wall at a time; 3x360 lasers wrap the whole room. They run from about $35 to $499 for DEWALT's 3x360 green kit.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT Line Laser, Self-Leveling, Cross Line, Red Beam (DW088K)
products.verdict: The highest-rated and most-reviewed laser here: a tough cross-line laser with a 1-meter drop rating, IP54 sealing, a built-in magnetic bracket, 1/8-inch accuracy at 30 feet and a 3-year warranty. Works with a detector out to 165 feet.
products.best_for: Cabinets, tile and trim where a laser has to survive a jobsite.
products.skip_if: You work in bright rooms; green beams are easier to see.

products.name: Lusweimi Laser Level with 50" Tripod, Self Leveling Green Cross Line Laser, 4 AA Batteries & Pouch
products.verdict: The cheapest laser here, and it still has a green beam, ±1/9-inch accuracy at 33 feet, a tilt alarm and a 50-inch tripod.
products.best_for: Hanging pictures and shelves for under $35.
products.skip_if: You need to work outdoors; no pulse mode is listed.

products.name: RockSeed Cross Line Laser Level, Self-Leveling, Rotatable 360 Degree, 40 Inch Tripod (LV1GT)
products.verdict: A best-selling budget cross-line laser with a 40-inch tripod, a rotating base, IP54 sealing and a 2-year service promise.
products.best_for: Indoor DIY at the lowest price.
products.skip_if: You want a green beam; the Lusweimi has one for a dollar less.

products.name: Fanttik D2 Pocket Green Laser Level for Picture Hanging and Home DIY
products.verdict: A pocket-size 0.56 lb green laser that charges by USB-C and runs about 10 hours, with a magnetic bracket and a pulse mode that reaches 164 feet with a receiver.
products.best_for: Homeowners who want a small, rechargeable green laser.
products.skip_if: You need a tripod; it comes with a magnetic bracket only.

products.name: Motovera Self Leveling Laser Level 100ft, Green Cross Line with Tripod, Pulse Function, IP54 (LL-T2)
products.verdict: The best-selling laser here: a green cross-line with four brightness settings, a pulse mode, IP54 sealing, a 30-inch drop rating, a tripod and a 24-month warranty.
products.best_for: A green laser with tripod and pulse mode under $40.
products.skip_if: Rating matters most; at 4.2 stars it's the lowest-rated pick.
pros: Green beam, pulse mode, 4 brightness levels
cons: Accuracy figure not shown on the listing

products.name: IKOVWUK Laser Level with 12 Green Lines, 3x360°, Built-in 5200 mAh Li-ion Battery
products.verdict: The best-rated budget 3x360: one horizontal and two vertical 360-degree green planes that wrap the room, a remote, pulse mode, a 5,200 mAh battery and an 18-month warranty.
products.best_for: Whole-room layout (ceilings, chair rails, wall-to-wall tile) on a budget.
products.skip_if: You only hang things on one wall; a cross-line laser is simpler.

products.name: Alloyman Laser Level with Tripod, 4x360° Self Leveling, 16 Green Lines (ALT16-20)

specs.in_box: Tripod, 2 batteries, charger, remote, magnetic stand, target plate

products.verdict: The most complete kit here: 4x360 green lines (including a floor plane), two rechargeable batteries, a tripod, a magnetic swivel stand, a remote and a target plate, for the same price as the IKOVWUK.
products.best_for: Floor and ceiling layout with everything in the box.
products.skip_if: You want a stronger track record; it's 4.3 stars.

products.name: BOSCH GLL50-20G 50 Ft Green-Beam Self-Leveling Cross-Line Laser Level
products.verdict: A brand-name green cross-line laser with IP55 sealing, a magnetic mount and Bosch's pendulum that blinks when out of level and locks for transport. Runs on AAs or an optional Bosch battery.
products.best_for: A compact brand-name green laser for interior work.
products.skip_if: Accuracy matters; 5/16 in at 30 ft is the loosest figure listed here.
pros: IP55, the best sealing after DEWALT's IP65

products.name: Klein Tools 93CPLG Compact Self-Leveling Laser Level, 100-Foot
products.verdict: A compact brand-name 3x360 green laser from Klein with a 100-foot range, a built-in rechargeable battery and a tilt mode for angled lines.
products.best_for: Electricians and remodelers who want a brand-name 3x360 for well under DEWALT's price.
products.skip_if: You'd rather swap batteries; this one is built in.

products.name: DEWALT Laser Level 360 Self Leveling, 3 Way Green, 12V MAX with 2.0Ah Battery, Charger and Case (DW089LG)

specs.accuracy: ±3 mm at 10 m (about 1/8 in at 33 ft)

products.verdict: The pro's 3x360: green planes, ±3 mm at 10 m, IP65 sealing, a locking pendulum, full-time pulse mode for a detector, a magnetic bracket with two thread sizes and a 3-year warranty. Runs on DEWALT 12V batteries.
products.best_for: Contractors laying out whole rooms every day.
products.skip_if: You're a homeowner; a $70 3x360 covers occasional jobs.
pros: ±3 mm at 10 m with 3x360 green planes

avoid.name: AikTryee Laser Level Line Tool, Cross Line Laser Leveler Beam Tool with 8ft Tape
avoid.flag: Not self-leveling; you level it by eye
avoid.verdict: A $10 laser pointer with bubble vials, sold as a laser level. For $25 more, the Lusweimi actually levels itself and lists its accuracy.
reasons: It isn't self-leveling. You line up a bubble vial by eye while it's stuck to the wall, so the line is only as level as your read of the bubble, which is exactly the error a laser level is supposed to remove.
The listing gives no accuracy figure at all, even though it's sold for cabinets and tile, the jobs where 1/8 inch matters.
It projects the line from where it's mounted on the wall, so it can't throw a level line across a room or onto an opposite wall like the self-leveling lasers above.

buyers_guide.a: A cross-line laser projects one horizontal and one vertical line on the wall in front of it, which covers pictures, shelves and a run of cabinets. A 3x360 laser wraps level and plumb lines around the whole room, which helps with ceilings, wall-to-wall tile and framing.
Green beams look about 2 to 4 times brighter to the eye, so they're easier to see in lit rooms and at distance. Red lasers cost less and run longer on batteries.
A pendulum inside swings the laser level by itself within about 3-4 degrees. If you set it on an uneven surface beyond that, it blinks to warn you. Lock the pendulum before moving it.
Outdoors or in bright sun you often can't see the beam. Pulse mode makes the laser flash at a rate a laser detector (sold separately) can pick up, extending the range to 150 feet or more.

buyers_guide.q: How accurate does a laser level need to be?
buyers_guide.a: About 1/8 inch at 30 feet is the common standard and fine for cabinets and tile. Many budget lasers don't publish an accuracy figure at all; check one against a known level line before relying on it.
